chunks: Then proceed to al-Safa and stand upon it until you can see the House and face the corner in which is the Stone. Praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, and mention as much as you can of His blessings and the goodness He has done to you. Then say:
"There is no deity except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is powerful over all things" three times.
And you say: "O Allah, I ask You for pardon, well-being, and certainty in this world and the Hereafter" three times.
And you say: "O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire" three times.

And you say: al-hamdu lillah one hundred times; Allahu akbar one hundred times; subhan Allah one hundred times; la ilaha illa Allah one hundred times; astaghfir Allah wa atubu ilayh one hundred times; and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad one hundred times.
And you say: "O He who does not disappoint His supplicant, and whose gift does not run out, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and grant me refuge from the Fire by Your mercy."
And supplicate for yourself with whatever you wish, and let your standing on al-Safa the first time be longer than the others.

Then descend and stop at the fourth step facing the Ka'bah and say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, its trial, its estrangement, its loneliness, its darkness, its narrowness, and its hardship. O Allah, shade me in the shade of Your Throne on the day when there is no shade except Your shade."

Then descend from the step while your back is uncovered and say: "O Lord of pardon, O He who commands pardon, O He who is most worthy of pardon, O He who rewards for pardon, pardon, pardon, pardon. O Generous, O Noble, O Near, O Far, restore Your blessing upon me, and employ me in Your obedience and Your good pleasure."

Then walk with tranquility and dignity until you come to the minaret, which is the edge of the place of sa'y, then hasten with the fullest stride of your gait, and say: "In the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah, forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know; indeed You are the Mightiest, the Most Generous, and guide me to that which is most upright. O Allah, my deed is weak, so multiply it for me and accept it from me. O Allah, for You is my sa'y, and through You are my power and strength, so accept my deed, O He who accepts the deed of the Godwary."

When you pass Zuqaq al-'Attarin, stop the brisk pace and walk calmly and with dignity, and say: "O Possessor of favor, abundance, generosity, blessing, and munificence, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and forgive my sins; indeed none forgives sins except You, O Generous One."

When you come to al-Marwah, ascend it and stand until the House becomes visible to you. Supplicate as you supplicated on al-Safa, ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for your needs, and say in your supplication: "O He who commands pardon, O He who rewards for pardon, O He who indicates pardon, O He who beautifies pardon, O He who rewards for pardon, O He who loves pardon, O He who gives for pardon, O He who pardons through pardon, O Lord of pardon, pardon, pardon, pardon."

And beseech Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and weep. If you are not able to weep, then make yourself weep. Strive to bring forth tears from your eyes even if like the head of a fly, and exert yourself in supplication.
Then descend from al-Marwah to al-Safa while walking. When you reach Zuqaq al-'Attarin, hasten with the fullest stride of your gait to the first minaret next to al-Safa.
When you reach it, stop the brisk pace and walk until you come to al-Safa. Stand upon it, face the House with your face, and say the like of what you said in the first round.
Then descend to al-Marwah and do what you had done, and say the like of what you had said in the first round until you come to al-Marwah.

So go between al-Safa and al-Marwah in seven circuits. Your standing on al-Safa will be four times and on al-Marwah four times, while the sa'y between them is seven, beginning with al-Safa and ending with al-Marwah.

Whoever leaves off the brisk pace during the sa'y until he has gone into part of the place should not turn his face around; rather, he returns backward until he reaches the place where he left off the brisk pace, then he hastens from there to the place where he should stop it, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.عَذَابِ ٱلْقَبْرِ: the punishment of the grave from which refuge is sought
key_terms.ٱلسَّعْيُ: the ritual walking and brisk movement between al-Safa and al-Marwah
key_terms.ٱلصَّفَا: al-Safa, the hill from which the sa'y begins
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْتِ: the Ka'bah, which is faced and viewed during the rite
key_terms.ٱلْعَفْوَ: pardon and forgiveness sought repeatedly from Allah
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْوَةَ: al-Marwah, the hill at which the sa'y ends
key_terms.ٱلْهَرْوَلَةَ: the brisk pace or hurried gait in the designated part of sa'y

ai.seo_question: What should be recited and done during the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah in hajj?
ai.summary: This passage outlines the recommended acts, supplications, and invocations during the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah in hajj. It combines devotional remembrance, requests for forgiveness and mercy, and procedural guidance for movement and conduct throughout the rite.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
PROCEEDING TO AL-SAFA
Then proceed to Safa and stand upon it until you can see the Kaaba. Face the corner containing the Black Stone, praise Allah (swt), glorify Him, and remember His blessings and the good He has bestowed upon you as much as you can. 
Then say:
"There is no deity except Allah (swt), alone without partner. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is capable of all things." 
Repeat this three times.
Say:
"O Allah (swt), I ask You for pardon, well-being, and certainty in this world and the Hereafter." Repeat this three times.
Say:
"Our Lord (azj), grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." Repeat this three times.
Then say:
•	Alhamdulillah (All praise is due to Allah (swt)) – 100 times.
•	Allahu Akbar (Allah (swt) is the Greatest) – 100 times.
•	SubhanAllah (swt) (Glory be to Allah (swt)) – 100 times.
•	La ilaha illa Allah (swt) (There is no deity but Allah (swt)) – 100 times.
•	Astaghfirullah wa atubu ilayh (I seek forgiveness from Allah (swt) and turn to Him in repentance) – 100 times.
•	Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad 100 times.
Then say:
"O One who does not disappoint those who ask Him, and whose generosity does not diminish, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and protect me from the Fire through Your mercy."
Supplicate for yourself with whatever you desire, and let your first standing at Safa be longer than the subsequent ones.
Then descend and stop at the fourth step while facing the Kaaba, and say:
"O Allah (swt), I seek refuge in You from the torment of the grave, its trials, its isolation, its desolation, its darkness, its narrowness, and its distress. O Allah (swt), shade me under the shadow of Your Throne on the Day when there is no shade except Your shade."
Then descend from the step while uncovering your back, and say:
"O Lord (azj), pardon me. O You who commands forgiveness, O You who is most deserving of forgiveness, O You who rewards for forgiveness, forgive me, forgive me, forgive me. O Generous One, O Noble One, O Near One, O Distant One, restore Your blessings upon me, and employ me in Your obedience and for what pleases You."
[Walking and Sa'i Between Safa and Marwah]
Walk with tranquility and dignity until you reach the minaret at the beginning of the Sa'i path. At that point, begin running (Sa’i) with a steady pace, and say:
"In the name of Allah (swt), Allah (swt) is the Greatest. O Allah (swt), bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. O Allah (swt), forgive, have mercy, and overlook what You know, for You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous. Guide me to that which is most upright. O Allah (swt), my deeds are weak, so multiply them for me and accept them from me. O Allah (swt), my Sa’i is for You, and my reliance and strength are by You, so accept my deeds, O One who accepts the deeds of the righteous."
When you pass the Zuqaq al-Attarin (the Perfumer’s Alley), stop running, walk with tranquility and dignity, and say:
"O Possessor of favor, grace, generosity, and bounty, O Giver and Benefactor, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and forgive my sins. Indeed, none forgives sins except You, O Generous One."
When you reach Marwah, ascend it and stand until the Kaaba becomes visible to you. Supplicate as you did on Safa and ask Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for your needs. Say in your supplication:
"O One who commands forgiveness, O One who rewards for forgiveness, O One who guides to forgiveness, O One who adorns forgiveness, O One who rewards for forgiveness, O One who loves forgiveness, O One who grants forgiveness, O One who forgives through forgiveness, O Lord (azj), forgive, forgive, forgive."
Humble yourself before Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. Cry if you can; if not, try to mimic crying, and strive to let tears flow from your eyes, even as small as the size of a fly’s head. 
Intensify your supplications.
Then descend from Marwah toward Safa while walking. When you reach the Zuqaq al-Attarin, begin running steadily to the first minaret near Safa. 
Upon reaching it, stop running and walk with tranquility until you arrive at Safa. Stand on it, face the Kaaba, and repeat what you said during the first round.
Then descend toward Marwah and repeat what you did and said during your previous rounds. 
Continue to do so, going between Safa and Marwah for seven circuits, standing on Safa four times and on Marwah four times. The Sa’i between them will be seven circuits, starting at Safa and ending at Marwah.
If you omit running during a part of the Sa’i, do not turn your face away; instead, return backward (al-qahqara) to the point where you left off, and begin running again from there to the designated place where you should stop. May Allah (swt), the Most High, facilitate it for you.
